Day 32 of 100 · Infrastructure Automation

Ansible Roles

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityInfrastructure AutomationPublished journey entry

Roles break large playbooks into reusable units with conventional locations for tasks, handlers, defaults, templates and files.

Architecture / mental model

site playbook → roles → tasks / handlers / templates / defaults / files

How it works

A role gives related automation a predictable structure. Instead of one playbook accumulating every responsibility, web-server logic, database logic and common host setup can evolve independently.

Role defaults provide low-precedence configurable values, while role tasks describe the behavior. This separation makes a role reusable without making its internals unreadable.

The published Day 32 teaser promised Galaxy next, but the journey later paid that teaser debt at Day 39. The blog preserves that history rather than pretending the sequence never bent.

Hands-on reference

ansible-galaxy role init roles/web
ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini site.yml

Verification

Run the role through a small top-level playbook, inspect handler behavior and confirm a second run converges cleanly.

Field note / gotcha

A role can become a dumping ground if responsibilities are not bounded. Reusability comes from a coherent purpose, not simply moving files into `roles/`.

Security considerations

Keep role defaults non-secret and make privileged tasks obvious. Reusable automation also reuses mistakes at scale.

What I learned

Structure is operational leverage when it makes behavior easier to reason about and test.

Evidence note: Published video/carousel evidence. Historical teaser debt recorded forward and paid at Day 39. The blog expands the technical explanation; it does not claim every paragraph is verbatim from the original social post.
